Rashi on Pesachim 105a:11:1.hebrew: כבוד יום וכבוד לילה - אם (יש) לו יין הרבה לסעודה אחת או מיני מגדים, יניחם עד היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:11:1.english: The honor of the day and the honor of the night - If he has plenty of wine for one meal, or types of delicacies, he should leave them until the day.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:1:1.english: [This is] difficult for Ulla - Who began with "Blessed" and did not conclude [with "Blessed"].

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:1:2.hebrew: הודאה היא - ואין בה הפסק דבר אחר — לא הפסק תחנה ולא הפסק ריצוי. הלכך, בפתיחתן סגי, ולא דמו לברכת קידוש שצריך לספר בשבח שבת, וברכת יוצר אור שיש בה הפסק תחנה, כגון "ברחמיך הרבים", וברכת אבות, יש בה רצוי; לפיכך צריך לפתוח ולסיים בשבחו של מקום:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:1:2.english: It is thanksgiving - and there is no interruption of another matter in it — neither an interruption of supplication nor an interruption of appeasement. Therefore, their opening [alone] suffices, and they are not like the blessing of Kiddush, [in] which one must recount the praise of Shabbat; nor the blessing of Yotzer Or, which has an interruption of supplication, such as "in Your abundant mercies"; nor the blessing of Avot, [which] has appeasement in it — therefore, one must open and conclude with the praise of the Omnipresent.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:1.english: They were sitting at a meal - On Shabbat eve, and they prolonged it until it grew dark.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:2.english: And we will interrupt - By removing the table.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:3.english: And we will establish it - [Meaning,] our meal.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:4.english: For Shabbat - For the sake of Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:5.english: You do not need - to interrupt [the meal] by removing the table in order to distinguish between a weekday meal and a Shabbat meal.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:6.hebrew: שבת היא קבעתה - מעצמה היא חשובה סעודת שבת ונבדלת מסעודת חול, ודי לכם בפריסת מפה וקידוש:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:2:6.english: Shabbat itself establishes it - By itself it is considered a Shabbat meal and is distinguished from a weekday meal, and spreading a cloth [over the bread] and [reciting] Kiddush are sufficient for you.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:3:1.hebrew: כשם שקובעת למעשר - אפילו אכילת עראי דשבת חשובה קבע למעשר, במסכת ביצה (ד' לד:):
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:3:1.english: Just as [Shabbat] establishes for tithes - Even casual eating on Shabbat is considered a set [meal] with regard to tithes, [as taught] in Tractate Beitzah (34b).

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:3:2.hebrew: כך קובעת לקידוש - שאסור לטעום עד שיקדש, אלמא משחשיכה היא חשובה סעודת שבת מאליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:3:2.english: So [Shabbat] establishes [the obligation] for kiddush - That it is forbidden to taste [anything] until one recites kiddush; thus, once it becomes dark, it is considered a Shabbat meal on its own.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:4:1.hebrew: כך - יציאתה קובעת להבדלה, שאם יושבים על השלחן וחשיכה במוצאי שבת, אסורין לאכול עד שיבדילו:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:4:1.english: So - [Shabbat's] departure establishes [the obligation] for havdalah, [meaning] that if they are sitting at the table and it becomes dark at the conclusion of Shabbat, they are forbidden to eat until they recite havdalah.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:5:1.hebrew: והני מילי - דלהבדלה אינה קובעת לאפסוקי סעודתא, אבל אתחולי לא מתחלינן משחשיכה עד שיבדילו:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:5:1.english: And this applies - that for Havdalah, it does not establish [an obligation] to interrupt a meal; however, we may not begin [a meal] once it has grown dark until they recite Havdalah.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:5:2.hebrew: הני מילי - דאין מפסיקין לאכילה, אבל לשתיה לאו דבר חשוב הוא ומפסקי:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:5:2.english: This applies - That we do not interrupt for eating, but for drinking, it is not a significant matter and they interrupt.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:6:1.hebrew: ולא אמרן - דלא מתחלי אלא בחמרא ושיכרא, אבל מיא לית לן בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:6:1.english: And we did not say - that they do not begin [drinking] except with wine and beer, but [with] water, we have no [problem] with it.

Rashi on Pesachim 105a:9:1.hebrew: הזכרה בברכת המזון - של שבת, רצה והחליצנו; וביום טוב, יעלה ויבא:
Rashi on Pesachim 105a:9:1.english: Mention in Grace after Meals - [The mention] of Shabbat [is] Retzei ve-hachalitzeinu, and on a Festival, Ya'aleh ve-yavo.

Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:1:1.hebrew: קשיא לעולא - לפירוש הקונטרס דפירש לעיל דלא אמר אלא "המבדיל בין קודש לחול" ותו לא — קשה: מאי ס"ד דמקשה? הא פשיטא דלברכת הפירות דמיא, דאין לך קצרה יותר מזו! ועוד: לימא דסבר עולא כר' יהודה הנשיא, דמשמע נמי דלא הוי חתים? ונראה דעולא אמר נמי כל שאר הבדלות, ואישתיק בלא חתימה; וס"ד דמקשה: כיון דארוכה היא קצת, הוה ליה למיחתם ב"ברוך", מידי דהוה אקידוש שחותמין בה אע"ג דהודאה היא, כיון שיש בה אריכות קצת. ומשני דדמיא שפיר לברכת פירות. וכן משמע, דרב יהודה לא היה שואל אלא לידע אם יחתום, או כרב או כשמואל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:1:1.english: This is difficult for Ulla - According to Rashi's explanation above, that [Ulla] only recited "Who separates between sacred and profane" and nothing more, this is difficult: what did the questioner think? It is obvious that it is comparable to a blessing over fruits, for you have none shorter than this! And furthermore, let [the Gemara] say that Ulla holds like Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, [whose view] also implies that he would not conclude [with "Blessed"]? Rather, it appears that Ulla also recited all the other separations [in Havdalah], and [then] stopped without a concluding blessing; and the questioner thought that since it is somewhat lengthy, he ought to conclude with "Blessed," just like Kiddush, where we conclude [with "Blessed"] even though it is [a blessing of] praise, since it has some length. And [the Gemara] answers that it is indeed comparable to a blessing over fruits. And so too it is implied, for Rav Yehuda was only asking in order to know whether he should conclude [with "Blessed"], whether like Rav or like Shmuel:

Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:3:1.hebrew: כך קובעת לקידוש - שאסור לאכול בלא קידוש, אפילו התחיל לאכול מבעוד יום. וה"נ קובעת למעשר אפי' התחיל לאכול עראי מבעוד יום, כדאמרינן בסוף המביא כדי יין (ביצה ד' לה.): "היה אוכל באשכול וחשכה לו שבת — רבי אליעזר אומר: יגמור, רבי יהושע אומר: לא יגמור":
Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:3:1.english: So [Shabbat] establishes [the requirement] for kiddush - That it is forbidden to eat without [reciting] kiddush, even if one began eating while it was still day. And so too it establishes [a fixed meal] for tithes, even if one began eating casually while it was still day, as we say at the end of [the chapter] Hamevi Kadei Yayin (Beitzah 35a): "If one was eating from a cluster [of grapes] and Shabbat fell upon him — Rabbi Eliezer says: He may finish [it]; Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not finish [it]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:5:1.hebrew: והנ"מ דאכלו ושתו מעיקרא - משמע שהיו אוכלים בשבת סמוך לחשיכה, ותימה, שלא נהגו לאכול בין מנחה למעריב. וגם ר"ת כעס על רבינו משולם שהנהיג לאכול בין מנחה למעריב, דאמר במדרש: "השותה מים בשבת בין השמשות גוזל את קרוביו המתים", וכתב שפעם אחת אירע מעשה בלותיר ובא לידי סכנה. ובקושי התירו ערב יום הכפורים לאכול אחר וידוי משום שכרות, וגם תשעה באב שחל להיות בשבת ונדחה התירו בקושי. ויש לדחות: דמיירי הכא שהתחילו בהיתר, ובאמצע סעודה התפללו מנחה, והיכא דהתחילו בהיתר מותר להשלים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:5:1.english: And this applies [only] when they ate and drank beforehand - This implies that they used to eat on Shabbat close to nightfall, and [this is] astonishing, for it is not customary to eat between Minchah and Ma'ariv. Moreover, Rabbeinu Tam was angry at Rabbeinu Meshullam, who instituted the custom of eating between Minchah and Ma'ariv, for it says in the Midrash: "One who drinks water on Shabbat at twilight robs his deceased relatives," and he wrote that once an incident occurred in Lotharingia and [someone] came into danger. And only with difficulty did they permit eating after the confession on the eve of Yom Kippur because of [concern for] drunkenness, and likewise [when] Tisha B'Av fell on Shabbat and was postponed [to Sunday], they permitted [eating then] only with difficulty. However, one can deflect [this difficulty by explaining] that here [the Gemara] is speaking [of a case] where they began permissibly [before Minchah], and in the middle of the meal they prayed Minchah, and where they began permissibly, it is permitted to finish.

Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:5:2.hebrew: אבל לשתיה מפסיקין - פירוש: שתיה בלא סעודה, דאין בה קביעות, ולכך מפסיקין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:5:2.english: But for drinking, one interrupts - Explanation: drinking without a meal, as it has no permanence, and therefore one interrupts.

Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:7:1.hebrew: לא קפדי אמיא - וברייתא דכל הטועם מיתתו באסכרה, לא מוקמי אמיא. ומיתתו באסכרה — מדה כנגד מדה הוא: משביע גרונו — יחנק. ואסכרה במקום חנק, כדאמרינן (כתובות ד' ל:): מי שנתחייב חנק — או טובע בנהר או מת בסרונכי, והיינו אסכרה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 105a:7:1.english: They were not particular with regard to water - And the Baraita of "whoever tastes [anything], his death will be through askara" — they do not establish [it as applying] to water. And "his death will be through askara" is measure for measure: one who sates his throat shall be strangled. And askara is in place of strangulation, as we say (Ketubot 30b): "One who became liable to strangulation either drowns in a river or dies of serunkhei" — and that is askara.
